where: Section 3, bullet point "Select the candidate with the smallest metric"
problem: The statement is true for error metrics (e.g., RMSE, MAE) but false for score metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1). It can mislead students to pick the wrong model for classification tasks.
fix: Clarify: "Select the candidate with the smallest error metric (e.g., RMSE, MAE) or the largest score metric (e.g., accuracy, F1)."

where: Section 2, sentence "Some syllabi label these as \"evaluation metrices\""
Exam traps, bullet "In leave‑one‑out CV, the computation time grows linearly with n"
problem: The description is misleading. LOOCV requires training a model n times, so the total cost grows roughly proportional to n times the cost of training on n‑1 samples, which can be O(n²) for many algorithms.
fix: Rewrite as: "In leave‑one‑out CV, the computation time grows proportionally to n times the cost of training a model, which can become very high for large n."
